battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists a 400 V architecture for the Leaf 75 kWh pack the Eclipse Sportback shares.

battery.preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Leaf sibling: Nissan Canada 2026 kit has a manual battery heater on all grades (navigation trigger only on some); no Mitsubishi page mentions preconditioning, so the lowest common feature is assumed.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Leaf sibling on the same platform: Nissan Canada 2026 kit gives a 7.2 kW onboard charger; Mitsubishi states no AC kW (J1772 port, Level 1/2).

dc_max_kw.notes: "up to 150 kW" at NACS/Tesla Superchargers.

published_10_80_min.notes: About 35 minutes 10-80% under optimal conditions.

charge_port.notes: NACS port (DC) on the passenger side; a separate J1772 port on the driver side handles AC (Canadian release for the same North American car).
InsideEVs (US outlet): NACS on the passenger-side fender, J1772 on the driver side; US car.

supercharger_access.notes: "access to Tesla's Supercharger network" (Canadian release).
InsideEVs: charges at Tesla Superchargers directly.

battery.capacity_gross_kwh.notes: "16 kWh" total capacity, 88 cells (2016 press kit); Mitsubishi Canada history page: 16-kWh pack. Same pack 2012-2017 (LEV50 cells, LEV50N from 2013 at the same capacity per Wikipedia).

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: 330 V nominal (2016 press kit; Guide Auto Canada 330 V); mapped to the 400v class (the schema has no lower class).

battery.capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Toyota says only "full capacity of 41.8 kWh" in Extended Mode (Standard Mode 35 kWh); Toyota does not label it gross.

battery.capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Green Car Reports: "41.8 kilowatt-hours of usable capacity"; Wikipedia: 41.8 kWh usable. Standard Mode (default) charges to 35 kWh per Toyota, so the everyday usable figure is lower.

battery.chemistry.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia (RAV4 EV): pack, electronics and powertrain "similar to" the Tesla Model S, about 4,500 Panasonic cells; Wikipedia (Model S): 18650 cells with a nickel-cobalt-aluminum cathode. Inference only: a Tesla-designed pack with Model S-type cells; neither Toyota nor Wikipedia names the RAV4 EV cell chemistry.

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Wikipedia: 386 V lithium-ion pack (class 400v).

battery.preconditioning.notes: Estimated: The Toyota 2012 pressroom page describes charging (240 V/40 A, about six hours) with a liquid-cooled pack and no battery-warming or preconditioning feature; the car has no DC charging, so DC preconditioning does not apply.

ac_max_kw.notes: Green Car Reports: the Tesla-designed charger "can charge at up to 10 kilowatts" (Wikipedia: 9.6 kW / 10 kW).

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia: only a J1772 240 V 40 A input; DC quick charge appears only as a third-party aftermarket upgrade (Quick Charge Power, 48 kW CHAdeMO); neither Toyota nor Green Car Reports mentions DC charging. Same car 2012-2014.

charge_port.notes: Wikipedia: "Production models use the SAE J1772 charging standard", 240 V 40 A input (US only, no DC port).

supercharger_access.notes: Estimated: No DC port and a pre-NACS Tesla-built car with a J1772 inlet; no Tesla or Toyota adapter programme found.
